newsitem.title: FRANCE: French brothers probed for murders of four girls.
newsitem.headline: French brothers probed for murders of four girls.

text.p: A judge on Saturday remanded two French brothers in custody on suspicion that they strangled four student girls in a crime that prompted calls for the restoration of the guillotine.

Blandine Lejeune, a lawyer for the victims' relatives, said the investigating magistrate ordered the two scrap dealer brothers, one a convicted murderer and the other a convicted rapist, formally probed for suspected multiple rape and murder.

Peggy, 20, and her 17-year-old sister Amelie, Isabelle, 20, and her sister Audrey, 17, had gone missing 11 days ago during a carnival evening in the Channel port of Boulogne. Their family names were not released.

The bodies, wearing fancy carnival dresses, were found hastily buried in the sand near a concrete bunker built by German forces during World War Two on a beach outside the village of Dannes, where the suspects live, 10 km (six miles) from Boulogne.
Police said the girls, who disappeared in the early hours of February 12, were apparently killed on the following evening.

Lejeune said they appeared to have been kidnapped after a dance and were strangled on the sand dunes. She said investigators were trying to establish how two men could have overpowered and killed the four women.

Prosecutor Gerald Lesigne named the suspects as Jean-Louis Jourdain, 37, and his brother Jean-Michel, 34. He said the elder was freed in 1995 after serving 11 years of a 15-year prison term for strangling a teenage girl to death. The younger was released in 1994 after serving eight years of a 10-year term for rape.
Investigators said they had blamed each other for the killings.
They were driven to prison through a crowd clamouring for the restoration of the death penalty, which was abolished 16 years ago. Police did not disclose where they were taken for security reasons.

Media reports said the two suspects lived in poverty, eking a living selling scrap iron. Police drove their relatives to an undisclosed destination after the father of two of the girls drove by the suspects' house, shouting he would burn it down.
Neigbours posted the pictures of the murdered girls on the ramshackle house with the word "Murderers" scribbled in red ink.
The mother of Peggy and Amelie said she would "save franc after franc to buy a pistol" and get revenge.

Thousands of neighbours in the Outreau suburb of Boulogne where the girls lived cancelled a children's festival and staged a silent march, some wearing white ribbons in what they said was a call for the death penalty.

The killings, unprecedented in recent years, shocked the country. "Slaughtered", the popular daily France-Soir screamed in a banner headline above pictures of the four girls smiling. The tabloid Le Parisien published their names on a black front page recalling a death notice.

Following a series of sex murders, and in the wake of Belgium's child murder scandal, the French government has tabled a bill to increase the punishment of sex offenders and institute medical control of rapists after they are released from prison.
From Bucharest, where he is on an official visit, French President Jacques Chirac has said he was "horrified and stunned by this act of savagery" and promised justice would be done.
In a happy ending to other disappearances which had caused anxiety in France, two teenage girls missing in London since last Wednesday were reunited with their families.
They told police they had missed their coach home and slept rough for two nights because they spoke no English and were too scared to approach anyone.
